# 御製歷象考成

**ID:** KR3f0018
**Custom ID:** ZB3f0019

**Extent:** (16) 卷
**Base edition:** WYG

## Authors / Editors
- 允祿 (清朝) 奉敕撰 1695 - 1767
- 何國宗 (清朝) 奉敕撰

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Lìxiàng kǎochéng*, in 42 *juàn* (16 + 10 + 16: Upper Edition + Lower Edition + Tables), is the astronomical-calendrical core of the great Kāngxī-Yōngzhèng-period imperial synthesis *Lǜlì yuānyuán* 律歷淵源 (Foundations of Music and Astronomy, 100 *juàn* total). Chartered by the Kāngxī emperor in Kāngxī 52 (1713) and completed under Yōngzhèng in Yōngzhèng 2 (1724), the work supersedes the Wànlì-Chóngzhēn-period [KR3f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0013) *Xīnfǎ suànshū* — explicitly correcting it on a series of specific technical points — and constitutes the new official-canonical Chinese astronomical-calendrical handbook of the high Qīng. It was the working basis of the *Qīntiānjiān* (Imperial Astronomical Bureau) until the further revision in [KR3f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0019) *Lìxiàng kǎochéng hòubiān* (1742) which introduced Keplerian elliptical orbits.

The work's tripartite structure:
- **Upper Edition (上編 *shàngbiān*)** — *Kuítiān chájì* 揆天察紀 ("Surveying-Heaven, Examining-the-Calendrical-Threads"): in 16 *juàn*, the theoretical-physical foundations — celestial geometry, the spherical-trigonometric apparatus, the cosmological framework, the geometric account of solar/lunar/planetary motion.
- **Lower Edition (下編 *xiàbiān*)** — *Míngshí zhèngdù* 明時正度 ("Clarifying-Time, Rectifying-Degrees"): in 10 *juàn*, the procedural-computational methods — the sequential procedures (*bùfǎ* 步法) for sun, moon, planets, eclipses, conjunctions.
- **Tables (表 *biǎo*)**: in 16 *juàn*, the numerical *lìchéng* (ready-reckoner) tables.

Front matter includes the *Yùzhì Lǜlì yuānyuán xù* 御製律歷淵源序 (Yōngzhèng's preface dated October 1723, the official imperial declaration of the project) and the personnel-list *Zhímíng* 職名 (with the full Yōngzhèng-2 / 1724 staff roster). The Sìkù 提要 (composed Qiánlóng 49 / 1784) frames the work as Kāngxī's specifically-commissioned correction of the limitations of the *Xīnfǎ suànshū*, accomplished against the background of the early-Qīng influx of Western mathematical-astronomical knowledge.

**Abstract**

Composition window: 1713 (Kāngxī 52, the imperial chartering of the *Méngyǎng zhāi* and the formal beginning of the project) – 1724 (Yōngzhèng 2, the year of completion-and-printing). The principal compilation took place under Kāngxī's personal direction (1713–1722); the final editorial revision and printing were completed under Yōngzhèng (1722–1724), with Yōngzhèng's preface dated October 1723.

The work's significance:

(a) **Successor and corrective to the *Xīnfǎ suànshū***: the *Lìxiàng kǎochéng* explicitly positions itself as the refinement of the late-Míng [KR3f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0013) *Xīnfǎ suànshū*, on the basis of (i) the more accurate measurements made under the early-Qīng *Qīntiānjiān* (notably the obliquity-of-the-ecliptic measurement of 23°29'30", reducing Tycho's value by 2 arcminutes); (ii) the better understanding of the European mathematical-astronomical tradition acquired through the post-1690s influx of Jesuit mathematicians like Antoine Thomas, Joachim Bouvet, Jean-François Gerbillon, and others; and (iii) the methodological maturation of the imperially-sponsored Kāngxī mathematical academy, under which Chinese mathematicians (Méi Wéndǐng's circle, then his grandson Méi Juéchéng, then Hé Guózōng and Míngāntú) became autonomous interpreters rather than mere transmitters of European material.

(b) **The 提要's six itemized corrections**: the 提要's enumeration of six specific technical corrections to the *Xīnfǎ suànshū* — the obliquity measurement, the equation-of-time decomposition, the *báipíng xiàngxiàn* solar-eclipse method, the moon-body coordinate system for lunar-eclipse positions, the geocentric reformulation of Tychonic planetary theory, and the simplified spherical-trigonometric apparatus — is one of the most precise late-imperial Chinese accountings of the *progress* of mathematical astronomy across one century. The 提要's careful citation-by-item invites comparison with the immediate-precursor [KR3f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0013) 提要 and frames the *Lìxiàng kǎochéng* as the realization of the late-Míng project's potential.

(c) **The geocentric vs. heliocentric question**: the 提要's explicit defense of geocentrism — claiming that Tycho's heliocentric placement of Venus and Mercury was merely "*an empty/clever computational method*" while the planets in fact orbit the Earth — reflects the standard Jesuit-Chinese consensus of the period. The Jesuit mission's continuing political-theological commitment to geocentrism (until the 1690s, when papal pressure on the Galileo question briefly relaxed) had constrained what could be transmitted; the Kāngxī court's mathematicians, working with the materials they had, naturally followed the same geocentric framework. The full transition to heliocentrism in Chinese state astronomy would come only in the 1730s-1740s with the *Hòubiān* [KR3f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0019) and its Keplerian elliptical orbits — though even there, formally, the mathematical framework remains compatible with either geocentric or heliocentric interpretation.

(d) **The synthetic *Lǜlì yuānyuán* project**: the 100-juan *Lǜlì yuānyuán* trilogy (*Lìxiàng kǎochéng* + *Lǜlǚ zhèngyì* + *Shùlǐ jīngyùn*) is the most ambitious imperial-scientific synthesis in late-imperial Chinese history. By bringing astronomy, music, and mathematics into a single integrated curriculum — and by explicitly grounding all three in the integration of European-and-Chinese sources — Kāngxī claimed for the imperial throne the role of supreme arbiter-and-synthesizer of natural philosophy. The Yōngzhèng preface's claim that "*even specialist named-houses cannot peep at one part-in-ten-thousand*" of the work's refinement articulates the ideology of the imperial synthesis as transcending all merely partial scholarship.

The work's institutional life was substantial: it served as the *Qīntiānjiān*'s working handbook from 1724 until the [KR3f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0019) *Hòubiān* of 1742, a period of eighteen years. After the *Hòubiān* the *Lìxiàng kǎochéng* was retained as foundational reference work — its tables and procedures continuing to inform Qīng calendrical practice in detail — but the *Hòubiān*'s elliptical-orbit reform progressively superseded it for the most accurate eclipse-and-planetary computations. The *Sìkù*-preserved recension is the original 1724 Yōngzhèng-2 imperial printing.

For the broader Kāngxī-Yōngzhèng-Qiánlóng synthesis-project, see [KR3f0019](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0019) (the Qián-lóng-period Keplerian revision) and [KR3f0020](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0020) (the Qián-lóng-period instrument-and-star catalog). For the late-Míng predecessor, see [KR3f0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR3/KR3f/KR3f0013). For the principal authors, see [允祿](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%85%81%E7%A5%BF) and [何國宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E5%9C%8B%E5%AE%97).
